# Finance Policy — Draft

**Organization:** [Church name]  
**Effective date:** [Date]  
**Approved by:** [Board or governing body]  
**Policy owner:** [Treasurer or finance lead]  
**Review date:** [Date]

*This is a starting template, not legal or accounting advice. Fill in the bracketed items, adapt it to your church’s governing documents and local requirements, and have your accountant and appropriate legal adviser review it before adoption.*

## 1. Purpose and scope

This policy establishes controls for receiving, safeguarding, spending, recording, and reporting the church’s funds. It applies to board members, staff, ministry leaders, volunteers, and anyone authorized to handle church money or financial records.

The church will use its funds only for authorized organizational purposes and will maintain complete, accurate, and timely financial records.

## 2. Roles and oversight

- **Governing body:** Approves the annual budget, this policy and its changes; reviews financial reports; and oversees financial controls.
- **Treasurer or finance lead:** Maintains or oversees the books, prepares reports, monitors the budget, and arranges timely reconciliations.
- **Authorized approvers:** Review and approve expenses and payments under the approval limits in this policy.
- **Bookkeeper:** Records transactions and maintains supporting documents. The bookkeeper may not approve their own expenses or payments.
- **All fund handlers:** Follow this policy, protect financial information, and promptly report suspected errors, misuse, or fraud.

No one may approve a payment to themselves. When practical, separate authorization, payment, and recording duties among different people.

## 3. Budget and financial planning

The governing body will approve an annual budget before the start of each fiscal year. The budget should include anticipated income, expenses, reserves, and any designated or restricted funds.

The finance lead will report actual results against the budget to the governing body at least [monthly/quarterly]. Material variances or unbudgeted commitments require approval under the limits below and should be documented.

## 4. Spending and payment approval

Church funds may be spent only for legitimate church purposes, within the approved budget or with additional approval.

| Amount or type of commitment | Required approval |
|---|---|
| Up to **[amount]** | [Role or approver] |
| **[amount]–[amount]** | [Two approvers or governing-body designees] |
| Above **[amount]**, unbudgeted, or a contract/recurring commitment | [Governing body or designated committee] |

- Approvals must be obtained before a purchase or commitment is made.
- Payments must have an invoice, receipt, contract, or other appropriate supporting documentation.
- The person requesting a payment must not be its sole approver.
- Payments to a board member, staff member, or related party require disclosure and approval by disinterested approvers, with the decision recorded in the minutes.
- Blank checks and pre-signed payment instruments are prohibited.
- Payments should be made through traceable methods where practical. Cash payments require a receipt and written explanation.

## 5. Reimbursements

A person seeking reimbursement must submit an itemized expense report with receipts and the ministry purpose within **[number] days** of the expense.

The claimant may not approve their own reimbursement. Reimbursements require approval by **[approver/role]** and must comply with the church’s approved budget and applicable tax rules. Any exception must be documented and approved by someone other than the claimant.

## 6. Bank accounts and financial access

- Bank accounts must be held in the church’s legal name.
- Account signers and online banking users must be approved by the governing body and reviewed at least annually and whenever roles change.
- Online banking access must be individual, protected by strong authentication where available, and removed promptly when no longer needed.
- Transfers between church accounts require approval by **[one/two]** authorized persons.
- Personal funds must not be mixed with church funds.
- New accounts, loans, credit facilities, or changes to signers require governing-body approval.

## 7. Donations and other receipts

- Donations and income must be recorded promptly, accurately, and in the appropriate account or fund.
- Cash and checks should be counted by **two unrelated people** when practical. Both counters should document the count, and deposits should be made promptly.
- A person who receives funds should not be the only person to count, record, and reconcile them.
- Donation acknowledgments and tax receipts will be issued in accordance with applicable law. The church will not promise a donor tax treatment it cannot substantiate.
- Donor records and payment information must be kept confidential and accessed only by people who need them for their roles.
- Contributions designated for a specific purpose will be handled consistently with the church’s stated donation terms and applicable law. If a designation cannot be honored, the church will seek appropriate guidance before reallocating the funds.

## 8. Cash handling and events

Each event or activity collecting cash must use a documented counting and deposit process. Two people should verify the amount collected, record any discrepancies, and secure the funds until deposited. Cash should not be used for personal loans or undocumented advances.

## 9. Credit and debit cards

Cards may be issued only with governing-body or delegated approval. Cardholders must use cards only for authorized church expenses, keep receipts, submit expense records by **[deadline]**, and never share cards or credentials. Cash advances and personal purchases are prohibited unless specifically authorized and documented.

## 10. Financial records and reconciliations

The church will maintain records sufficient to support its financial statements, donor acknowledgments, tax filings, and governance decisions. Records will be stored securely and retained for **[period, subject to local law and professional advice]**.

Bank and card accounts must be reconciled at least monthly by someone who does not have sole control over the related transactions. A separate reviewer should examine and document the reconciliation. Differences or suspicious transactions must be investigated and reported to the governing body.

## 11. Financial reporting and restricted funds

The finance lead will provide the governing body with financial reports at least **[monthly/quarterly]**, including income and expenses compared with budget, cash balances, and balances of restricted or designated funds.

Restricted funds must be tracked separately in the accounting records and used only in accordance with the applicable restriction. The church will not treat restricted funds as available for general expenses.

## 12. Conflicts of interest and suspected misuse

Anyone with a personal or financial interest in a transaction must disclose it before discussion or approval and must not participate in the decision except to provide requested information. The disclosure and decision must be documented.

Anyone who suspects theft, misuse, a significant accounting error, or a breach of this policy should report it promptly to **[treasurer/board chair/contact]**. Reports will be handled discreetly and reviewed by people without a conflict. Retaliation for raising a concern in good faith is prohibited.

## 13. Exceptions, enforcement, and review

Exceptions must be approved in advance by **[governing body or delegated authority]**, documented with the reason, and reported in the next financial review. Violations may result in removal of financial access or other action by the governing body.

The governing body will review this policy at least annually and update it when the church’s operations or requirements change.
